metadata.dcterms:abstract:
The Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support Member States in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. Developed in response to World Health Assembly mandates and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and WHO’s Triple Billion targets, the strategy outlines a shared vision for improving health and well-being through accessible, affordable, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. It emphasizes the importance of strong governance, interoperability, ethical use of data, privacy protection, workforce capacity-building and investment in digital infrastructure to support national health priorities and universal health coverage.
The document establishes four strategic objectives: promoting global collaboration and knowledge exchange; advancing the implementation of national digital health strategies; strengthening governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels; and advocating people-centred health systems enabled by digital technologies. It also presents guiding principles, an implementation framework and monitoring mechanisms to support countries in developing interoperable digital health ecosystems. Particular attention is given to addressing barriers faced by low- and middle-income countries and ensuring that digital transformation contributes to equitable, effective and resilient health systems.
